$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 4,\,1\le z\le 12-2x-2y}.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Notice that we have a three-dimensional type I region.

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{1}^{12-2x-2y}\,dz\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{4}[z]_{z=1}^{z=12-2x-2y}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{4}12-2x-2y-1\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{4}11-2x-2y\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[11y-2xy-{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=4}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}44-8x-16\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}-8x+28\,dx \\  & ={[-4{x}^{2}+28x]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =-4+28-0 \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-03f2be2d-3077-50fe-b425-7498945d27f1"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-03f2be2d-3077-50fe-b425-7498945d27f1" :answer-field/id #uuid "03f2be2d-3077-50fe-b425-7498945d27f1" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-2b56129c-0df0-54af-906e-0e2a10719caa" :answer-field/choices ["answer-6a682a9c-2f58-50f5-aa7f-1f1a6a470892" "answer-2b56129c-0df0-54af-906e-0e2a10719caa" "answer-26f453de-fdf1-55b9-a976-f40753f1a395" "answer-b002bf51-05e0-5a47-b8cd-c23d9bd55718" "answer-d0dfa491-fc3b-502e-9e30-73d701d08848"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6a682a9c-2f58-50f5-aa7f-1f1a6a470892" :answer/id #uuid "6a682a9c-2f58-50f5-aa7f-1f1a6a470892" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "16" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2b56129c-0df0-54af-906e-0e2a10719caa" :answer/id #uuid "2b56129c-0df0-54af-906e-0e2a10719caa" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "24" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-26f453de-fdf1-55b9-a976-f40753f1a395" :answer/id #uuid "26f453de-fdf1-55b9-a976-f40753f1a395" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "28" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b002bf51-05e0-5a47-b8cd-c23d9bd55718" :answer/id #uuid "b002bf51-05e0-5a47-b8cd-c23d9bd55718" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{16}{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d0dfa491-fc3b-502e-9e30-73d701d08848" :answer/id #uuid "d0dfa491-fc3b-502e-9e30-73d701d08848" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{25}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-89162549-49ec-507f-b56c-dea9e66a6c30" :question/id #uuid "89162549-49ec-507f-b56c-dea9e66a6c30" :question/math-academy-id "q-161654" :question/problem "Find the volume of the solid $R$ given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,1-x\le y\le 1+x,\,0\le z\le xy}.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Notice that we have a three-dimensional type I region.

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1-x}^{1+x}{\int }_{0}^{xy}\,dz\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1-x}^{1+x}[z]_{z=0}^{z=xy}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1-x}^{1+x}xy\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=1-x}^{y=1+x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{x}{2}((1+x)^{2}-(1-x)^{2})\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{x}{2}((1+2x+{x}^{2})-(1-2x+{x}^{2}))\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{x}{2}(4x)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2{x}^{2}\,dx \\  & ={[\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-3acdc6ec-2a12-547a-88f2-73cc8411f0a8"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-3acdc6ec-2a12-547a-88f2-73cc8411f0a8" :answer-field/id #uuid "3acdc6ec-2a12-547a-88f2-73cc8411f0a8" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-bc206240-eb24-501d-9e9e-fc7fd50a7902" :answer-field/choices ["answer-6ec6ec01-733e-5f02-af23-9cc8caaac3a2" "answer-d8ffd103-8f74-5398-842a-0cf2cb86197a" "answer-b9a79b99-32b0-5d67-90f5-be49d7031cdb" "answer-bc206240-eb24-501d-9e9e-fc7fd50a7902" "answer-7908b9c9-85f1-5fb7-8993-c1b1c1be6014"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6ec6ec01-733e-5f02-af23-9cc8caaac3a2" :answer/id #uuid "6ec6ec01-733e-5f02-af23-9cc8caaac3a2" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d8ffd103-8f74-5398-842a-0cf2cb86197a" :answer/id #uuid "d8ffd103-8f74-5398-842a-0cf2cb86197a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b9a79b99-32b0-5d67-90f5-be49d7031cdb" :answer/id #uuid "b9a79b99-32b0-5d67-90f5-be49d7031cdb" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{10}{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-bc206240-eb24-501d-9e9e-fc7fd50a7902" :answer/id #uuid "bc206240-eb24-501d-9e9e-fc7fd50a7902" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{2}{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-7908b9c9-85f1-5fb7-8993-c1b1c1be6014" :answer/id #uuid "7908b9c9-85f1-5fb7-8993-c1b1c1be6014" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{5}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-e95b54dd-6268-5c5c-a490-a7470ea8eb6e" :question/id #uuid "e95b54dd-6268-5c5c-a490-a7470ea8eb6e" :question/math-academy-id "q-40305" :question/problem "Find the volume of the solid $R,$ given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,-1\le z\le 1,\,1\le y\le {x}^{2}+2{z}^{2}+2}.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Notice that we have a three-dimensional type III region.

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{{x}^{2}+2{z}^{2}+2}\,dy\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}[y]_{y=1}^{y={x}^{2}+2{z}^{2}+2}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}({x}^{2}+2{z}^{2}+2)-1\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{x}^{2}+2{z}^{2}+1\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[({x}^{2}+1)z+\frac{2{z}^{3}}{3}]}_{z=-1}^{z=1}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}+1)(1-(-1))+\frac{2}{3}({1}^{3}-(-1)^{3})\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}2{x}^{2}+\frac{10}{3}\,dx \\  & ={[\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}+\frac{10}{3}x]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =(\frac{2}{3}(2)^{3}+\frac{10}{3}(2))-0 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-4313eb1e-43e2-5591-a760-a6cd81db0c05"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-4313eb1e-43e2-5591-a760-a6cd81db0c05" :answer-field/id #uuid "4313eb1e-43e2-5591-a760-a6cd81db0c05" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-af4d0a8b-1782-5c16-9feb-e54dff10e54a" :answer-field/choices ["answer-ab25cad1-cd37-5991-b571-041028cd4125" "answer-af4d0a8b-1782-5c16-9feb-e54dff10e54a" "answer-81bffb26-ac25-55bf-8e70-fc8fa0c1f3e2" "answer-6594fd8f-7b74-5439-ac33-7bfcb0497e40" "answer-34c83166-7494-5134-b177-dcd7f8751b56"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-ab25cad1-cd37-5991-b571-041028cd4125" :answer/id #uuid "ab25cad1-cd37-5991-b571-041028cd4125" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "10" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-af4d0a8b-1782-5c16-9feb-e54dff10e54a" :answer/id #uuid "af4d0a8b-1782-5c16-9feb-e54dff10e54a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "12" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-81bffb26-ac25-55bf-8e70-fc8fa0c1f3e2" :answer/id #uuid "81bffb26-ac25-55bf-8e70-fc8fa0c1f3e2" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "6" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6594fd8f-7b74-5439-ac33-7bfcb0497e40" :answer/id #uuid "6594fd8f-7b74-5439-ac33-7bfcb0497e40" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{14}{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-34c83166-7494-5134-b177-dcd7f8751b56" :answer/id #uuid "34c83166-7494-5134-b177-dcd7f8751b56" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{28}{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-9b5b7d1e-4726-5549-b494-2d265b26d8f0" :question/id #uuid "9b5b7d1e-4726-5549-b494-2d265b26d8f0" :question/math-academy-id "q-161661" :question/problem "Find the volume of the solid $R,$ given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 4,\,4\le z\le 8-x,\,0\le y\le 2-\frac{x}{2}}.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Notice that we have a three-dimensional type III region.

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{4}^{8-x}{\int }_{0}^{2-\frac{x}{2}}\,dy\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{4}^{8-x}[y]_{y=0}^{y=2-\frac{x}{2}}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{4}^{8-x}2-\frac{x}{2}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}(2-\frac{x}{2}){[z]}_{z=4}^{z=8-x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}(2-\frac{x}{2})(8-x-4)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}(2-\frac{x}{2})(4-x)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}8-4x+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}\,dx \\  & ={[8x-2{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{6}{x}^{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=4} \\  & =(8(4)-2(4)^{2}+\frac{1}{6}(4)^{3})-0 \\  & =\frac{32}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-e818f6e1-d129-5503-b9af-07473e5656ca"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-e818f6e1-d129-5503-b9af-07473e5656ca" :answer-field/id #uuid "e818f6e1-d129-5503-b9af-07473e5656ca" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-2d6a5b58-75ec-53ab-a1d2-eb0bf32cf642" :answer-field/choices ["answer-77a79373-1a09-54a3-a0eb-c907112d07e8" "answer-b1cec824-ea51-56e4-b35a-71eecbf948d6" "answer-fe6589a0-a2f1-5e12-abad-5d645468e2ab" "answer-2d6a5b58-75ec-53ab-a1d2-eb0bf32cf642" "answer-9abd54bf-c0ef-5909-85ca-4e4eaf1cbed8"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-77a79373-1a09-54a3-a0eb-c907112d07e8" :answer/id #uuid "77a79373-1a09-54a3-a0eb-c907112d07e8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "24" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b1cec824-ea51-56e4-b35a-71eecbf948d6" :answer/id #uuid "b1cec824-ea51-56e4-b35a-71eecbf948d6" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "36" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-fe6589a0-a2f1-5e12-abad-5d645468e2ab" :answer/id #uuid "fe6589a0-a2f1-5e12-abad-5d645468e2ab" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{18}{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2d6a5b58-75ec-53ab-a1d2-eb0bf32cf642" :answer/id #uuid "2d6a5b58-75ec-53ab-a1d2-eb0bf32cf642" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{32}{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9abd54bf-c0ef-5909-85ca-4e4eaf1cbed8" :answer/id #uuid "9abd54bf-c0ef-5909-85ca-4e4eaf1cbed8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{33}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-341b5b80-395a-52ac-87f9-9ef65cfdd0e9" :question/id #uuid "341b5b80-395a-52ac-87f9-9ef65cfdd0e9" :question/math-academy-id "q-161658" :question/problem "Find the volume of the solid $R,$ given by

R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le z\le y,\,0\le x\le 3-y-z}.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Notice that we have a three-dimensional type II region.

\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}{\int }_{0}^{3-y-z}\,dx\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}[x]_{x=0}^{x=3-y-z}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}3-y-z\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[(3-y)z-\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=y}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(3-y)y-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3y-\frac{3}{2}{y}^{2}\,dy \\  & ={[\frac{3}{2}{y}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}-\frac{1}{2}-0 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}

Notice that our solid can be written as the type II region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le 2-\frac{1}{3}y-\frac{1}{2}z},
$$

where $D$ is the projection of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane.

To find the top boundary curve of $D$ in the form $z=z(y),$ we substitute $x=1$ into the equation $x=2-\frac{1}{3}y-\frac{1}{2}z:$

$$
1=2-\frac{1}{3}y-\frac{1}{2}z\,⟹\,z=2-\frac{2}{3}y
$$

Then, we have

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,\,0\le z\le 2-\frac{2}{3}y},
$$

as shown below.

![](images/ea/ea8b8397163309a11aa478fcc21ab53ee293c19f0d77a93b5c3d3472bb0eba70.png)

Hence, the type II representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,\,0\le z\le 2-\frac{2}{3}y,\,\,0\le x\le 2-\frac{1}{3}y-\frac{1}{2}z}.
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-2y/3}{\int }_{0}^{2-y/3-z/2}dx\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-2y/3}[x]_{x=0}^{x=2-y/3-z/2}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-2y/3}(2-\frac{y}{3}-\frac{z}{2})-0\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-2y/3}2-\frac{y}{3}-\frac{z}{2}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{[(2-\frac{y}{3})z-\frac{{z}^{2}}{4}]}_{z=0}^{z=2-2y/3}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}((2-\frac{y}{3})(2-\frac{2y}{3})-\frac{1}{4}{(2-\frac{2y}{3})}^{2})-0\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(2-\frac{2y}{3})((2-\frac{y}{3})-\frac{1}{4}(2-\frac{2y}{3}))\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(2-\frac{2y}{3})(\frac{3}{2}-\frac{y}{6})\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}3-\frac{4y}{3}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}\,dy \\  & ={[3y-\frac{2{y}^{2}}{3}+\frac{{y}^{3}}{27}]}_{y=0}^{y=3} \\  & =(3(3)-\frac{2(3)^{2}}{3}+\frac{{3}^{3}}{27})-0 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-133b7b39-61d0-5df1-8fb5-ebbf0005ae7b"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-133b7b39-61d0-5df1-8fb5-ebbf0005ae7b" :answer-field/id #uuid "133b7b39-61d0-5df1-8fb5-ebbf0005ae7b" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-553cda93-dcb2-5e16-b4c0-6ae818e9e098" :answer-field/choices ["answer-8f8412c6-b5ae-5e4e-8894-ef77a1531b0b" "answer-bffefc4b-533b-5a59-a2a7-3d67fb1ca1ca" "answer-9680b5da-cca4-55bb-9bba-6bb3fc907b66" "answer-553cda93-dcb2-5e16-b4c0-6ae818e9e098" "answer-9081743f-8252-523c-aefd-cf033c9164c4"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8f8412c6-b5ae-5e4e-8894-ef77a1531b0b" :answer/id #uuid "8f8412c6-b5ae-5e4e-8894-ef77a1531b0b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-bffefc4b-533b-5a59-a2a7-3d67fb1ca1ca" :answer/id #uuid "bffefc4b-533b-5a59-a2a7-3d67fb1ca1ca" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9680b5da-cca4-55bb-9bba-6bb3fc907b66" :answer/id #uuid "9680b5da-cca4-55bb-9bba-6bb3fc907b66" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-553cda93-dcb2-5e16-b4c0-6ae818e9e098" :answer/id #uuid "553cda93-dcb2-5e16-b4c0-6ae818e9e098" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9081743f-8252-523c-aefd-cf033c9164c4" :answer/id #uuid "9081743f-8252-523c-aefd-cf033c9164c4" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "5" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-4ef656bf-166c-5181-a3cb-7a7a57c705a6" :question/id #uuid "4ef656bf-166c-5181-a3cb-7a7a57c705a6" :question/math-academy-id "q-161692" :question/problem "![](images/f7/f7fe261b981f8c97a123675d1385237d62cdbb8c9976dc8c3f1841f073e497de.png)

$$

$$

$$

What is ${a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f?$" :question/worked-solution "First, we need to determine the projection of the intersection of our surfaces onto the $xy$-plane. So, let's find where they intersect.

$$
\begin{aligned}2+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2} & =4+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} \\ 2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the projection of the intersection in the $xy$-plane is an ellipse.

Notice that our solid can be written as a type I region: 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,2+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}\le z\le 4+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}},
$$

where $D$ is the interior of the ellipse $2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=2.$ 

As a result, the volume of $R$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{2+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}}^{4+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\text{d}z]\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(4+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})-(2+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- the lower part $y=-\sqrt{2-2{x}^{2}},$ and

- the upper part $y=\sqrt{2-2{x}^{2}},$

for $-1\le x\le 1.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-\sqrt{2-2{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{2-2{x}^{2}}}\,2-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,dy\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f & ={(-\sqrt{2-2{x}^{2}})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{2-2{x}^{2}})}^{2}+(2-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}) \\  & =(2-2{x}^{2})+(2-2{x}^{2})+(2-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}) \\  & =6-6{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & =16-{z}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =16\end{aligned}
$$

So, the projection of the intersection in the $xz$-plane is a circle.

Notice that our solid can be written as a type III region: 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 16-{z}^{2}},

$$

- the lower part $z=-\sqrt{16-{x}^{2}},$ and

- the upper part $z=\sqrt{16-{x}^{2}},$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}16-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-4}^{4}{\int }_{-\sqrt{16-{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{16-{x}^{2}}}\,16-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,dz\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f(y,z) & ={(-\sqrt{16-{x}^{2}})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{16-{z}^{2}})}^{2}+(16-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}) \\  & =(16-{x}^{2})+(16-{x}^{2})+(16-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}) \\  & =48-3{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}.\end{aligned}

for $-2\le x\le 2.$

$$

$$
\textrm{Area}\ \!(D) = \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D} 1 \cdot \textrm d A = \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}  \ \textrm d A
$$

We have a similar result for triple integrals:

*If $R$ is a region in three-dimensional space, then the volume of $R$ is given by*

$$
\textrm{Volume}(R) = \iiint\limits_{R} \textrm{d}V.
$$

In other words, the volume of $R$ equals the triple integral of the function $f(x,y,z)=1$ over $R.$ 

For example, let's use triple integrals to find the volume of the rectangular prism shown below.

![](images/8f/8f9ab5db03f1cdf84ef484aca1ab89995237e7ef333c9b7c563d0080d317e981.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written in set-builder notation as

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 3 \big\}.
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}dz\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}dx\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}dy\cdot {\int }_{0}^{3}dz \\  & =(1-0)\cdot (2-0)\cdot (3-0) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** We get the same value using the formula for the volume of a rectangular prism:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\text{length}\cdot \text{width}\cdot \text{height} \\  & =1\cdot 2\cdot 3 \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Let's see some more examples." :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186129386 :activity/expected-seconds 1380.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

Notice that our solid can be written as the type II region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le 1+y+z},
$$

where

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane, shown below.

![](images/b4/b497e6ef73b5b16e11baa08819e9628d3b5e1f2ee4d05fbafec48f73e087cbf1.png)

Hence, the type II representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le 1+y+z}
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1+y+z}dx\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}[x]_{x=0}^{x=1+y+z}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(1+y+z)-0\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}1+y+z\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[(1+y)z+\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}1+y+\frac{1}{2}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{2}+y\,dy \\  & ={[\frac{3}{2}y+\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =(\frac{3}{2}+\frac{1}{2})-0 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-77f278fd-49bc-544f-84b1-fa3bfe926285"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-77f278fd-49bc-544f-84b1-fa3bfe926285" :answer-field/id #uuid "77f278fd-49bc-544f-84b1-fa3bfe926285" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-1c05b87c-0a2f-5b02-9732-195c4cebeb2f" :answer-field/choices ["answer-3efc03d6-4a00-528f-9d96-c985b96a5a27" "answer-1c05b87c-0a2f-5b02-9732-195c4cebeb2f" "answer-d74a887e-50b3-566c-a5b5-055f90be3eb9" "answer-52c8cce2-caca-5867-98e7-2a89cae75f20" "answer-ee22bbbb-c1bb-5206-b091-b3f1ee42854b"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3efc03d6-4a00-528f-9d96-c985b96a5a27" :answer/id #uuid "3efc03d6-4a00-528f-9d96-c985b96a5a27" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1c05b87c-0a2f-5b02-9732-195c4cebeb2f" :answer/id #uuid "1c05b87c-0a2f-5b02-9732-195c4cebeb2f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d74a887e-50b3-566c-a5b5-055f90be3eb9" :answer/id #uuid "d74a887e-50b3-566c-a5b5-055f90be3eb9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-52c8cce2-caca-5867-98e7-2a89cae75f20" :answer/id #uuid "52c8cce2-caca-5867-98e7-2a89cae75f20" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-ee22bbbb-c1bb-5206-b091-b3f1ee42854b" :answer/id #uuid "ee22bbbb-c1bb-5206-b091-b3f1ee42854b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{3}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-2c5e175a-7b49-566c-a1ad-cebab486783a" :question/id #uuid "2c5e175a-7b49-566c-a1ad-cebab486783a" :question/math-academy-id "q-161741" :question/problem "![](images/da/daedf62c68ba62dee844cf17efc2d767da47a06ceccaedde854779f542b90114.png)

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the front and right ones, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*" :question/worked-solution "![](images/7c/7c1738e97bc16a32f86d6901136afc4d9e288035d170fcd640db340ad36d19c5.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type II region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le 2-\frac{1}{3}y-\frac{1}{2}z},
$$

where $D$ is the projection of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane.

To find the top boundary curve of $D$ in the form $z=z(y),$ we substitute $x=1$ into the equation $x=2-\frac{1}{3}y-\frac{1}{2}z:$

$$
1=2-\frac{1}{3}y-\frac{1}{2}z\,⟹\,z=2-\frac{2}{3}y
$$

Then, we have

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,\,0\le z\le 2-\frac{2}{3}y},
$$

as shown below.

![](images/ea/ea8b8397163309a11aa478fcc21ab53ee293c19f0d77a93b5c3d3472bb0eba70.png)

Hence, the type II representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,\,0\le z\le 2-\frac{2}{3}y,\,\,0\le x\le 2-\frac{1}{3}y-\frac{1}{2}z}.
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-2y/3}{\int }_{0}^{2-y/3-z/2}dx\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-2y/3}[x]_{x=0}^{x=2-y/3-z/2}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-2y/3}(2-\frac{y}{3}-\frac{z}{2})-0\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-2y/3}2-\frac{y}{3}-\frac{z}{2}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{[(2-\frac{y}{3})z-\frac{{z}^{2}}{4}]}_{z=0}^{z=2-2y/3}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}((2-\frac{y}{3})(2-\frac{2y}{3})-\frac{1}{4}{(2-\frac{2y}{3})}^{2})-0\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(2-\frac{2y}{3})((2-\frac{y}{3})-\frac{1}{4}(2-\frac{2y}{3}))\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(2-\frac{2y}{3})(\frac{3}{2}-\frac{y}{6})\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}3-\frac{4y}{3}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}\,dy \\  & ={[3y-\frac{2{y}^{2}}{3}+\frac{{y}^{3}}{27}]}_{y=0}^{y=3} \\  & =(3(3)-\frac{2(3)^{2}}{3}+\frac{{3}^{3}}{27})-0 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-133b7b39-61d0-5df1-8fb5-ebbf0005ae7b"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-133b7b39-61d0-5df1-8fb5-ebbf0005ae7b" :answer-field/id #uuid "133b7b39-61d0-5df1-8fb5-ebbf0005ae7b" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-553cda93-dcb2-5e16-b4c0-6ae818e9e098" :answer-field/choices ["answer-8f8412c6-b5ae-5e4e-8894-ef77a1531b0b" "answer-bffefc4b-533b-5a59-a2a7-3d67fb1ca1ca" "answer-9680b5da-cca4-55bb-9bba-6bb3fc907b66" "answer-553cda93-dcb2-5e16-b4c0-6ae818e9e098" "answer-9081743f-8252-523c-aefd-cf033c9164c4"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8f8412c6-b5ae-5e4e-8894-ef77a1531b0b" :answer/id #uuid "8f8412c6-b5ae-5e4e-8894-ef77a1531b0b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-bffefc4b-533b-5a59-a2a7-3d67fb1ca1ca" :answer/id #uuid "bffefc4b-533b-5a59-a2a7-3d67fb1ca1ca" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9680b5da-cca4-55bb-9bba-6bb3fc907b66" :answer/id #uuid "9680b5da-cca4-55bb-9bba-6bb3fc907b66" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-553cda93-dcb2-5e16-b4c0-6ae818e9e098" :answer/id #uuid "553cda93-dcb2-5e16-b4c0-6ae818e9e098" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9081743f-8252-523c-aefd-cf033c9164c4" :answer/id #uuid "9081743f-8252-523c-aefd-cf033c9164c4" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "5" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-4ef656bf-166c-5181-a3cb-7a7a57c705a6" :question/id #uuid "4ef656bf-166c-5181-a3cb-7a7a57c705a6" :question/math-academy-id "q-161692" :question/problem "![](images/f7/f7fe261b981f8c97a123675d1385237d62cdbb8c9976dc8c3f1841f073e497de.png)

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le 2+2y-z},

$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane, shown below.

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2+2y-z}dx\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}[x]_{x=0}^{x=2+2y-z}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2+2y-z)-0\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}2+2y-z\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[(2+2y)z-\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2+2y-\frac{1}{2}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{2}+2y\,dy \\  & ={[\frac{3}{2}y+{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =(\frac{3}{2}+1)-0 \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-9b3b1258-5fda-5712-badd-881fc05d24bd"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-9b3b1258-5fda-5712-badd-881fc05d24bd" :answer-field/id #uuid "9b3b1258-5fda-5712-badd-881fc05d24bd" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-d45c8daf-95fb-55e5-89c7-d36d75897c10" :answer-field/choices ["answer-2b03de32-d32b-50f3-9d81-a9356d8226fd" "answer-84e5b082-ea93-5227-8dcc-35b31f9f13c9" "answer-80809090-d5dd-5ad5-8948-4e33b67f495a" "answer-0846e1fd-4ddb-5928-9bfb-cd2dba987965" "answer-d45c8daf-95fb-55e5-89c7-d36d75897c10"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2b03de32-d32b-50f3-9d81-a9356d8226fd" :answer/id #uuid "2b03de32-d32b-50f3-9d81-a9356d8226fd" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-84e5b082-ea93-5227-8dcc-35b31f9f13c9" :answer/id #uuid "84e5b082-ea93-5227-8dcc-35b31f9f13c9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-80809090-d5dd-5ad5-8948-4e33b67f495a" :answer/id #uuid "80809090-d5dd-5ad5-8948-4e33b67f495a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-0846e1fd-4ddb-5928-9bfb-cd2dba987965" :answer/id #uuid "0846e1fd-4ddb-5928-9bfb-cd2dba987965" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{3}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d45c8daf-95fb-55e5-89c7-d36d75897c10" :answer/id #uuid "d45c8daf-95fb-55e5-89c7-d36d75897c10" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{5}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-bc1d5c0b-7b74-5ad3-bb28-1b0236b6db17" :question/id #uuid "bc1d5c0b-7b74-5ad3-bb28-1b0236b6db17" :question/math-academy-id "q-161698" :question/problem "![](images/59/599b5392add89a6a22eb6c2232fedbdd26704ebf849bb05d7de52a6d81dcfb6a.png)

Find the volume of the solid region above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the right one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*" :question/worked-solution "![](images/59/599b5392add89a6a22eb6c2232fedbdd26704ebf849bb05d7de52a6d81dcfb6a.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type III region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le 3-\frac{x}{2}-z},
$$

where

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 2}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane, shown below.

![](images/9e/9e7c6fad45d9d85bad5ca16a2000e4d44a1739ab70797e41ae94945a4ffb02ef.png)

Hence, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 3-\frac{x}{2}-z}
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3-x/2-z}dy\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}[y]_{y=0}^{y=3-x/2-z}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(3-\frac{x}{2}-z)-0\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}3-\frac{x}{2}-z\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[(3-\frac{x}{2})z-\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}((3-\frac{x}{2})(2)-\frac{{2}^{2}}{2})-0\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}4-x\,dx \\  & ={[4x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =(8-2)-0 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-7f638fd3-87cf-5489-b15f-bb90365aa5c7"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-7f638fd3-87cf-5489-b15f-bb90365aa5c7" :answer-field/id #uuid "7f638fd3-87cf-5489-b15f-bb90365aa5c7" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-07ab8e05-2f75-5f1a-81dd-e07557bc4267" :answer-field/choices ["answer-1c0c0737-e66b-54ce-a699-eb6eaa91aed3" "answer-adf7bc54-9182-550e-91a1-e85a8bb8a42a" "answer-18508c80-0e18-52e8-aaa1-c7e154a4a945" "answer-07ab8e05-2f75-5f1a-81dd-e07557bc4267" "answer-33546658-bf3e-5faf-af2d-8c9d52241a04"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1c0c0737-e66b-54ce-a699-eb6eaa91aed3" :answer/id #uuid "1c0c0737-e66b-54ce-a699-eb6eaa91aed3" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "10" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-adf7bc54-9182-550e-91a1-e85a8bb8a42a" :answer/id #uuid "adf7bc54-9182-550e-91a1-e85a8bb8a42a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "12" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-18508c80-0e18-52e8-aaa1-c7e154a4a945" :answer/id #uuid "18508c80-0e18-52e8-aaa1-c7e154a4a945" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "14" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-07ab8e05-2f75-5f1a-81dd-e07557bc4267" :answer/id #uuid "07ab8e05-2f75-5f1a-81dd-e07557bc4267" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "6" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-33546658-bf3e-5faf-af2d-8c9d52241a04" :answer/id #uuid "33546658-bf3e-5faf-af2d-8c9d52241a04" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "8" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186129766 :question/problem "Find the volume of the solid region enclosed by the $yz$-plane, the surface $x=6yz+12,$ and the planes $y=0,$ $y=2,$ $z=0,$ $z=1.$" :question/worked-solution "Notice that our solid can be written as a type II region:

$$
V={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{a(x)}^{b(x)}\,f(x,y)\,dy\,dx
$$

What is ${a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f?$" :question/worked-solution "First, we need to determine the projection of the intersection of our surfaces onto the $xy$-plane. So, let's find where they intersect.

$$
\begin{aligned}2+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2} & =4+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} \\ 2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the projection of the intersection in the $xy$-plane is an ellipse.

Notice that our solid can be written as a type I region: 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,2+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}\le z\le 4+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}},
$$

where $D$ is the interior of the ellipse $2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=2.$ 

As a result, the volume of $R$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{2+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}}^{4+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\text{d}z]\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(4+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})-(2+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the boundary of $D$ consists of 

- the lower part $y=-\sqrt{2-2{x}^{2}},$ and

- the upper part $y=\sqrt{2-2{x}^{2}},$

for $-1\le x\le 1.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-\sqrt{2-2{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{2-2{x}^{2}}}\,2-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,dy\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f & ={(-\sqrt{2-2{x}^{2}})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{2-2{x}^{2}})}^{2}+(2-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}) \\  & =(2-2{x}^{2})+(2-2{x}^{2})+(2-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}) \\  & =6-6{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-ca8f622f-5689-5e59-b05c-8fbe8f53d165"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id \begin{aligned}-7+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2} & =1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} \\ 2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =8\end{aligned}
$$

So, the projection of the intersection in the $xy$-plane is an ellipse.

Notice that our solid can be written as a type I region: 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,-7+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}\le z\le 1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}},
$$

where $D$ is the interior of the ellipse $2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=8.$ 

As a result, the volume of $R$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-7+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}}^{1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\text{d}z]\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})-(-7+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}8-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the boundary of $D$ consists of 

- the lower part $y=-\sqrt{8-2{x}^{2}},$ and

- the upper part $y=\sqrt{8-2{x}^{2}},$

for $-2\le x\le 2.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}8-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}{\int }_{-\sqrt{8-2{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{8-2{x}^{2}}}\,8-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,dy\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f & ={(-\sqrt{8-2{x}^{2}})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{8-2{x}^{2}})}^{2}+(8-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}) \\  & =(8-2{x}^{2})+(8-2{x}^{2})+(8-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}) \\  & =24-6{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-ea386800-ecda-5f25-a01e-e6b7ef7365e9"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-ea386800-ecda-5f25-a01e-e6b7ef7365e9" :answer-field/id #uuid "ea386800-ecda-5f25-a01e-e6b7ef7365e9" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-419aa363-49d4-5a7e-8648-41b4d89d3360" :answer-field/choices ["answer-5a35c9bc-b0cc-547d-b618-465e5dc40b31" "answer-419aa363-49d4-5a7e-8648-41b4d89d3360" "answer-c5d89b6f-0e3c-592b-8ec6-ea236b410b7f" "answer-2a53e873-260c-523d-86d2-7a180a1002fa" "answer-f1627d2e-6e9b-5b03-86e7-80be1ddf0ea8"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5a35c9bc-b0cc-547d-b618-465e5dc40b31" :answer/id #uuid "5a35c9bc-b0cc-547d-b618-465e5dc40b31" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "12-6{x}^{2}-6{y}^{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-419aa363-49d4-5a7e-8648-41b4d89d3360" :answer/id #uuid "419aa363-49d4-5a7e-8648-41b4d89d3360" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "24-6{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-c5d89b6f-0e3c-592b-8ec6-ea236b410b7f" :answer/id #uuid "c5d89b6f-0e3c-592b-8ec6-ea236b410b7f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "24-8{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2a53e873-260c-523d-86d2-7a180a1002fa" :answer/id #uuid "2a53e873-260c-523d-86d2-7a180a1002fa" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-f1627d2e-6e9b-5b03-86e7-80be1ddf0ea8" :answer/id #uuid "f1627d2e-6e9b-5b03-86e7-80be1ddf0ea8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186130410 :tutorial/content "Recall that the double Integral of the function $f(x,y) = 1$ over a domain $D\subset \mathbb R^2$ is simply the area of $D\mathbin{:}$

$$
\textrm{Area}\ \!(D) = \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D} 1 \cdot \textrm d A = \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}  \ \textrm d A
$$

We have a similar result for triple integrals:

*If $R$ is a region in three-dimensional space, then the volume of $R$ is given by*

$$
\textrm{Volume}(R) = \iiint\limits_{R} \textrm{d}V.
$$

In other words, the volume of $R$ equals the triple integral of the function $f(x,y,z)=1$ over $R.$ 

For example, let's use triple integrals to find the volume of the rectangular prism shown below.

![](images/8f/8f9ab5db03f1cdf84ef484aca1ab89995237e7ef333c9b7c563d0080d317e981.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written in set-builder notation as

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 3 \big\}.
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}dz\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}dx\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}dy\cdot {\int }_{0}^{3}dz \\  & =(1-0)\cdot (2-0)\cdot (3-0) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** We get the same value using the formula for the volume of a rectangular prism:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\text{length}\cdot \text{width}\cdot \text{height} \\  & =1\cdot 2\cdot 3 \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

"![](images/b0/b0645201b3726750226811e0c714dc09d3075021fcbb6ddd1525748e9539c02d.png)

Find the volume of the solid region above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the front one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*"] ["question-d44ebfc0-d493-5ede-9c33-adfa1ab81dd9" :question/worked-solution "![](images/c4/c4cf12ec9b53282620c1730f824c96d98e0b9dbabee0478bf258cf6c2741da81.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type II region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le 1+y+z},
$$

where

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane, shown below.

![](images/b4/b497e6ef73b5b16e11baa08819e9628d3b5e1f2ee4d05fbafec48f73e087cbf1.png)

Hence, the type II representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le 1+y+z}
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1+y+z}dx\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}[x]_{x=0}^{x=1+y+z}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(1+y+z)-0\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}1+y+z\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[(1+y)z+\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}1+y+\frac{1}{2}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{2}+y\,dy \\  & ={[\frac{3}{2}y+\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =(\frac{3}{2}+\frac{1}{2})-0 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-d44ebfc0-d493-5ede-9c33-adfa1ab81dd9" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["answer-field-77f278fd-49bc-544f-84b1-fa3bfe926285" :answer-field/id #uuid *Hint: All surfaces, except for the front and right ones, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*"] ["question-2c5e175a-7b49-566c-a1ad-cebab486783a" :question/worked-solution "![](images/7c/7c1738e97bc16a32f86d6901136afc4d9e288035d170fcd640db340ad36d19c5.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type II region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le 2-\frac{1}{3}y-\frac{1}{2}z},
$$

where $D$ is the projection of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane.

To find the top boundary curve of $D$ in the form $z=z(y),$ we substitute $x=1$ into the equation $x=2-\frac{1}{3}y-\frac{1}{2}z:$

$$
1=2-\frac{1}{3}y-\frac{1}{2}z\,⟹\,z=2-\frac{2}{3}y
$$

Then, we have

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,\,0\le z\le 2-\frac{2}{3}y},
$$

as shown below.

![](images/ea/ea8b8397163309a11aa478fcc21ab53ee293c19f0d77a93b5c3d3472bb0eba70.png)

Hence, the type II representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,\,0\le z\le 2-\frac{2}{3}y,\,\,0\le x\le 2-\frac{1}{3}y-\frac{1}{2}z}.
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-2y/3}{\int }_{0}^{2-y/3-z/2}dx\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-2y/3}[x]_{x=0}^{x=2-y/3-z/2}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-2y/3}(2-\frac{y}{3}-\frac{z}{2})-0\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-2y/3}2-\frac{y}{3}-\frac{z}{2}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{[(2-\frac{y}{3})z-\frac{{z}^{2}}{4}]}_{z=0}^{z=2-2y/3}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}((2-\frac{y}{3})(2-\frac{2y}{3})-\frac{1}{4}{(2-\frac{2y}{3})}^{2})-0\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(2-\frac{2y}{3})((2-\frac{y}{3})-\frac{1}{4}(2-\frac{2y}{3}))\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(2-\frac{2y}{3})(\frac{3}{2}-\frac{y}{6})\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}3-\frac{4y}{3}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}\,dy \\  & ={[3y-\frac{2{y}^{2}}{3}+\frac{{y}^{3}}{27}]}_{y=0}^{y=3} \\  & =(3(3)-\frac{2(3)^{2}}{3}+\frac{{3}^{3}}{27})-0 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-2c5e175a-7b49-566c-a1ad-cebab486783a" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["answer-field-133b7b39-61d0-5df1-8fb5-ebbf0005ae7b" :answer-field/id #uuid $$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-y+2z}dx\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}[x]_{x=0}^{x=2-y+2z}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}(2-y+2z)-0\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}2-y+2z\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[(2-y)z+{z}^{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=3}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}((2-y)(3)+{3}^{2})-0\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}15-3y\,dy \\  & ={[15y-\frac{3}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =(30-6)-0 \\  & =24.\end{aligned}

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le 2+2y-z},

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1}

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le 2+2y-z}

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2+2y-z}dx\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}[x]_{x=0}^{x=2+2y-z}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2+2y-z)-0\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}2+2y-z\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[(2+2y)z-\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2+2y-\frac{1}{2}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{2}+2y\,dy \\  & ={[\frac{3}{2}y+{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =(\frac{3}{2}+1)-0 \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-6e182344-0946-5483-a450-ce9ff2b36770" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["answer-field-9b3b1258-5fda-5712-badd-881fc05d24bd" :answer-field/id #uuid $$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le 3-\frac{x}{2}-z},

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 3-\frac{x}{2}-z}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{x+y}}\,dz\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}[z]_{z=0}^{z={e}^{x+y}}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{x+y}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{e}^{x+y}]_{y=0}^{y=1}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{x+1}-{e}^{x}\,dx \\  & ={[{e}^{x+1}-{e}^{x}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =({e}^{1+1}-{e}^{1})-({e}^{0+1}-{e}^{0}) \\  & ={e}^{2}-e-e+1 \\  & =(e-1)^{2}\end{aligned}

:question/problem "Find the volume of the solid region enclosed by the $xy$-plane and the plane $z=x+y+2,$ and the planes $x=-1,$ $x=0,$ $y=0,$ $y=1.$"] ["question-5ddd03f9-52bb-5aac-ab6f-e8e23245dd8b" :question/worked-solution "Notice that our solid can be written as a type I region: 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,-1\le x\le 0,\,\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le x+y+2}
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x+y+2}\,dz\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}[z]_{z=0}^{z=x+y+2}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}x+y+2\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{[(x+2)y+\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=1}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}x+2+\frac{1}{2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}x+\frac{5}{2}\,dx \\  & ={[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}x]}_{x=-1}^{x=0} \\  & =0-(\frac{1}{2}(-1)^{2}+\frac{5}{2}(-1)) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{5}{2} \\  & =2\end{aligned}

["question-3fb0f5ed-20e1-5a6f-bec1-d9ddd1ad73da" :question/math-academy-id "q-161703"] ["question-3fb0f5ed-20e1-5a6f-bec1-d9ddd1ad73da" :question/problem "Consider the solid enclosed between the paraboloids $z=2+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}$ and $z=4+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2},$ whose volume can be written in terms of double integrals, as follows:

$$
V={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{a(x)}^{b(x)}\,f(x,y)\,dy\,dx
$$

What is ${a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f?$"] ["question-3fb0f5ed-20e1-5a6f-bec1-d9ddd1ad73da" :question/worked-solution "First, we need to determine the projection of the intersection of our surfaces onto the $xy$-plane. So, let's find where they intersect.

$$
\begin{aligned}2+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2} & =4+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} \\ 2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the projection of the intersection in the $xy$-plane is an ellipse.

Notice that our solid can be written as a type I region: 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,2+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}\le z\le 4+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}},
$$

where $D$ is the interior of the ellipse $2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=2.$ 

As a result, the volume of $R$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{2+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}}^{4+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\text{d}z]\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(4+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})-(2+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the boundary of $D$ consists of 

- the lower part $y=-\sqrt{2-2{x}^{2}},$ and

- the upper part $y=\sqrt{2-2{x}^{2}},$

for $-1\le x\le 1.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-\sqrt{2-2{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{2-2{x}^{2}}}\,2-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,dy\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f & ={(-\sqrt{2-2{x}^{2}})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{2-2{x}^{2}})}^{2}+(2-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}) \\  & =(2-2{x}^{2})+(2-2{x}^{2})+(2-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}) \\  & =6-6{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-3fb0f5ed-20e1-5a6f-bec1-d9ddd1ad73da" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] ["answer-field-ca8f622f-5689-5e59-b05c-8fbe8f53d165" :answer-field/id #uuid What is ${a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f?$"] ["question-a2dc848f-1abc-53f8-b5eb-d94beb1dc593" :question/worked-solution "First, we need to determine the projection of the intersection of our surfaces onto the $xz$-plane. So, let's find where they intersect.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & =16-{z}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =16\end{aligned}
$$

So, the projection of the intersection in the $xz$-plane is a circle.

Notice that our solid can be written as a type III region: 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 16-{z}^{2}},
$$

where $D$ is the interior of the circle ${x}^{2}+{z}^{2}=16.$ 

As a result, the volume of $R$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{16-{z}^{2}}\text{d}y]\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(16-{z}^{2})-({x}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}16-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the boundary of $D$ consists of 

- the lower part $z=-\sqrt{16-{x}^{2}},$ and

- the upper part $z=\sqrt{16-{x}^{2}},$

for $-4\le x\le 4.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}16-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-4}^{4}{\int }_{-\sqrt{16-{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{16-{x}^{2}}}\,16-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,dz\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f(y,z) & ={(-\sqrt{16-{x}^{2}})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{16-{z}^{2}})}^{2}+(16-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}) \\  & =(16-{x}^{2})+(16-{x}^{2})+(16-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}) \\  & =48-3{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-a2dc848f-1abc-53f8-b5eb-d94beb1dc593" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] ["answer-field-130fe27f-0430-583d-a4a3-c1d6d680d596" :answer-field/id #uuid $$
\begin{aligned}-4+{x}^{2} & =5-{z}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =9\end{aligned}
$$

So, the projection of the intersection in the $xz$-plane is a circle.

Notice that our solid can be written as a type III region: 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,-4+{x}^{2}\le y\le 5-{z}^{2}},
$$

where $D$ is the interior of the circle ${x}^{2}+{z}^{2}=9.$ 

As a result, the volume of $R$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-4+{x}^{2}}^{5-{z}^{2}}\text{d}y]\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5-{z}^{2})-(-4+{x}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}9-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the boundary of $D$ consists of 

- the lower part $z=-\sqrt{9-{x}^{2}},$ and

- the upper part $z=\sqrt{9-{x}^{2}},$

for $-3\le x\le 3.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}9-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-3}^{3}{\int }_{-\sqrt{9-{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{9-{x}^{2}}}\,9-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,dz\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f & ={(-\sqrt{9-{x}^{2}})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{9-{x}^{2}})}^{2}+(9-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}) \\  & =(9-{x}^{2})+(9-{x}^{2})+(9-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}) \\  & =27-3{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-d28d127a-2ef1-5397-a112-fbe0142a6964" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] ["answer-field-25ccf850-549b-5aa0-8084-8546dd642420" :answer-field/id #uuid $$

So, the projection of the intersection in the $yz$-plane is an ellipse.

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,5{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}\le x\le 9-4{y}^{2}},

- the lower part $z=-\sqrt{9-9{y}^{2}},$ and

- the upper part $z=\sqrt{9-9{y}^{2}},$

for $-1\le y\le 1.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}9-9{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-\sqrt{9-9{y}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{9-9{y}^{2}}}\,9-9{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,dz\,dy.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

- the lower part $y=-\sqrt{8-2{x}^{2}},$ and

- the upper part $y=\sqrt{8-2{x}^{2}},$

for $-2\le x\le 2.$

$$

$$"] ["question-59448eff-6a38-5971-9e73-20a5809538bf" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] ["answer-field-ea386800-ecda-5f25-a01e-e6b7ef7365e9" :answer-field/id #uuid "answer-field-ea386800-ecda-5f25-a01e-e6b7ef7365e9"] [17592186235284 :knowledge-point/questions "question-59448eff-6a38-5971-9e73-20a5809538bf"] [17592186130410 :tutorial/content "Recall that the double Integral of the function $f(x,y) = 1$ over a domain $D\subset \mathbb R^2$ is simply the area of $D\mathbin{:}$

$$
\textrm{Area}\ \!(D) = \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D} 1 \cdot \textrm d A = \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}  \ \textrm d A
$$

We have a similar result for triple integrals:

*If $R$ is a region in three-dimensional space, then the volume of $R$ is given by*

$$
\textrm{Volume}(R) = \iiint\limits_{R} \textrm{d}V.
$$

In other words, the volume of $R$ equals the triple integral of the function $f(x,y,z)=1$ over $R.$ 

For example, let's use triple integrals to find the volume of the rectangular prism shown below.

![](images/8f/8f9ab5db03f1cdf84ef484aca1ab89995237e7ef333c9b7c563d0080d317e981.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written in set-builder notation as

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 3 \big\}.
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}dz\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}dx\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}dy\cdot {\int }_{0}^{3}dz \\  & =(1-0)\cdot (2-0)\cdot (3-0) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** We get the same value using the formula for the volume of a rectangular prism:

$$

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the top one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*" :question/worked-solution "![](images/75/75a76a2dbc34c889335e66623e12b686eb9a255ee0d67f9be0e3792f2650360c.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type I region

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (x,y) \in D, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 4-x-y \big\},
$$

where

$$
D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 2 \big\}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane, shown below.

![](images/e1/e19ffe6a0555851c2b05526272beb21dbcdc082a23a2e11809c661666efdf133.png)

Hence, the type I representation of $R$ is

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 4-x-y \big\}.
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

[{:db/id 17592186130098 :step/content {:db/id 17592186130410 :tutorial/content "Recall that the double Integral of the function $f(x,y) = 1$ over a domain $D\subset \mathbb R^2$ is simply the area of $D\mathbin{:}$

$$
\textrm{Area}\ \!(D) = \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D} 1 \cdot \textrm d A = \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}  \ \textrm d A
$$

We have a similar result for triple integrals:

> *If $R$ is a region in three-dimensional space, then the volume of $R$ is given by*
> 
> 
> $$
> \textrm{Volume}(R) = \iiint\limits_{R} \textrm{d}V.
> $$

In other words, the volume of $R$ equals the triple integral of the function $f(x,y,z)=1$ over $R.$ 

For example, let's use triple integrals to find the volume of the rectangular prism shown below.

![](images/8f/8f9ab5db03f1cdf84ef484aca1ab89995237e7ef333c9b7c563d0080d317e981.png)

Notice that our solid can be written in set-builder notation as

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 3 \big\}.
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}dz\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}dx\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}dy\cdot {\int }_{0}^{3}dz \\  & =(1-0)\cdot (2-0)\cdot (3-0) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** We get the same value using the formula for the volume of a rectangular prism:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\text{length}\cdot \text{width}\cdot \text{height} \\  & =1\cdot 2\cdot 3 \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Let's see some more examples." :tutorial/id #uuid "8b8f4748-190d-5fda-9a83-139e6a994d94" :tutorial/math-academy-id 4911 :tutorial/title "Introduction"} :step/id #uuid Building on the analytical framework established in the first course, students study orthogonality, multivariable integration, vector calculus theorems, and advanced methods for differential equations.
The course emphasizes mathematical structures that arise naturally in physics, including inner product spaces, orthogonal projections, integral theorems of vector calculus, and transform methods for solving differential equations. These tools provide the mathematical foundation for analyzing electromagnetic fields, wave phenomena, dynamical systems, and statistical models encountered in advanced physics courses." 17592186045417] [17592186046660 1009 "The course begins with the theory of projections in inner product spaces. Students study norms, inner products, orthogonality, and orthogonal complements in vector spaces over the real and complex numbers. Techniques such as orthogonal projections, the Gram–Schmidt process, and QR factorization allow vectors to be decomposed into orthogonal components. These ideas play a role in Fourier analysis, signal decomposition, and numerical methods used in physical simulations.
Students then explore quadratic forms and the diagonalization of symmetric matrices. The spectral theorem provides a geometric interpretation of symmetric transformations and leads to techniques for analyzing energy functions and stability in physical systems. Singular value decomposition is also introduced as a powerful matrix factorization with applications in numerical modeling and data analysis.
Applications of linear algebra follow, including least-squares methods for solving overdetermined systems. These methods arise when fitting theoretical models to experimental data and when approximating solutions to physical equations.
The course then develops multivariable integration in three dimensions. Students compute triple integrals over general regions and apply coordinate transformations such as cylindrical and spherical coordinates. These techniques allow physicists to compute quantities such as mass distributions, charge densities, and gravitational or electric potentials.
Students next study line integrals and surface integrals of scalar and vector fields. Concepts such as circulation, flux, and path independence lead to the fundamental theorems of vector calculus, including Green’s theorem, the divergence theorem, and Stokes’ theorem. These results form the mathematical framework underlying conservation laws and the differential and integral formulations of electromagnetic theory.
Applications of multivariable calculus follow, including vector mechanics and optimization. Students analyze motion using vector-valued functions, apply Newton’s second law to systems in the plane, and study work–energy relationships. Multiple integrals are used to compute mass, centers of mass, moments of inertia, and other physical quantities.
The course then returns to differential equations, extending earlier techniques to systems of linear differential equations. Students analyze dynamical systems using eigenvalues, phase portraits, and matrix methods, which appear in models of interacting systems such as coupled oscillators or predator–prey dynamics.
Laplace transforms are introduced as a powerful tool for solving linear differential equations with discontinuous inputs or initial conditions. Boundary value problems and Fourier series are then developed, providing mathematical techniques used to solve differential equations describing heat flow, vibrating strings, wave propagation, and other physical phenomena.
The course concludes with numerical methods for differential equations and advanced probability topics. Students analyze the accuracy and stability of numerical schemes used in computational physics and study multivariate probability distributions and the central limit theorem, which appear in We have a similar result for triple integrals:

> *If $R$ is a region in three-dimensional space, then the volume of $R$ is given by*
> 
> 
> $$
> \textrm{Volume}(R) = \iiint\limits_{R} \textrm{d}V.
> $$

In other words, the volume of $R$ equals the triple integral of the function $f(x,y,z)=1$ over $R.$ 

For example, let's use triple integrals to find the volume of the rectangular prism shown below.

![](images/8f/8f9ab5db03f1cdf84ef484aca1ab89995237e7ef333c9b7c563d0080d317e981.png)

Notice that our solid can be written in set-builder notation as

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 3 \big\}.
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}dz\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}dx\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}dy\cdot {\int }_{0}^{3}dz \\  & =(1-0)\cdot (2-0)\cdot (3-0) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** We get the same value using the formula for the volume of a rectangular prism:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\text{length}\cdot \text{width}\cdot \text{height} \\  & =1\cdot 2\cdot 3 \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$
